about: The one revision manifest for local acceptance (issue #67, H1). Every Go, first-party and toolchain pin the harness uses is here; harness/manifest.py validates it. Historical, policy and selective Go targets are separate entries: none of them is a relabelled copy of another, and old goldens keep their own recorded versions.

toolchain.go_source: go.mod of the newest Go target (8bba7a77)

historical.about: The revision the 50-case Claude wire collector was built against (harness/evidence/2026-10-02*.json.gz). Detects unintended regressions against that recording; it is not current-provider proof.

policy.about: AGENTS.md's frozen default reference for non-Codex behaviour. Go goldens under crates/*/tests/fixtures carry their own recorded versions; the harness does not run this revision and does not relabel any golden to it. Golden recording only: harness/run --target policy --golden captures golden_cases, whose Go side becomes a committed expectation (harness/expectations/) for behaviour v8.0.10 cannot answer. Such a run is never acceptance evidence by itself.

selective.about: The selective upstream target of docs/SELECTIVE-UPSTREAM-PLAN.md. Comparing against it does not adopt it: a difference is either a named expected divergence (pending feature, provider-first decision or harness boundary) or a failure.

codex.about: Go behaviour never decides a Codex payload, transport or identity; Codex has no Go differential group.

claude-differential.about: harness/fixtures.py cases(): the historical 50 Claude scenarios over the TLS collector.

selective-differential.about: The 50 Claude scenarios plus harness/fixtures.py selective_cases(): Grok and Muse over a plain-HTTP loopback upstream. TLS fingerprint emulation is not compared for them.

groups.about: Claude Messages and translated routes through the real router with a loopback mock; credential masking in the shared capture sink.
docs/codex/CONTRACT.md: the fixture manifest's provenance, and native HTTP, native WebSocket and translated routes against CaptureUpstream, byte for byte where the contract says so.
Grok through Responses, Chat Completions and Messages clients, buffered and streaming, against CaptureUpstream.
Muse through Responses, Chat Completions and Messages clients, buffered and streaming, against CaptureUpstream.
Removed providers (#49) and native plugins (#47) stay refused: routes, settings, model names and management writes.
Negative controls: the semantic checks fail on mutated captures.

invariants.about: Checked on every case and target, whatever divergence applies. Credential ownership and isolation, capture consistency and upstream write completion apply to both sides; the native-byte rules apply to cliproxy-rs. Every captured upstream request must finish writing its scripted reply (`write_result` complete) except in `upstream_write_failures`, whose client abandons the stream; there each side's write must still be a recorded collector outcome, and Go and Rust must agree.

rules.ledger: docs/DIFFERENCES-FROM-GO.md "Response header field-name case and order"
rules.rule: Downstream header fields are compared as case-insensitive names with ordered values; raw head bytes only need to agree with those parsed fields on each side.
Chunked downstream framing may split differently; each side's wire must decode to its own body, and bodies are compared byte for byte.
A Content-Length may differ only when each side's value equals its own body length and the bodies' difference is itself explained.
generated_headers values are masked only after matching their pattern on both sides.

masks.about: The only values a golden template or a generated JSON value may leave open. Each mask is narrow: `pattern` is what the value's text must match; `json_type` is the exact JSON type a generated value must have before it is masked; `decode` names a structural check (harness/golden.py); `record` finds it in a capture when a golden is recorded.
